questions.prompt: What key lifecycle benefit does the SwiftUI .task modifier offer over onAppear?

options.text: It automatically cancels running asynchronous tasks when the view disappears.
options.explanation: The .task modifier ties execution to the view presentation lifecycle and cancels work when the view is dismissed.

options.text: It forces network requests to execute synchronously on the main thread.
options.explanation: The modifier executes asynchronous tasks non-blockingly without freezing the UI thread.

options.text: It persists downloaded JSON files directly into SQLite local database storage.
options.explanation: The modifier does not manage disk persistence or database storage.

options.text: It disables cooperative task cancellation for all network operations.
options.explanation: The modifier relies on cooperative cancellation to stop work when the view leaves the screen.

questions.prompt: How does the .task(id:) modifier handle changes to its identity parameter?

options.text: It queues new work while allowing previous in-flight tasks to continue.
options.explanation: It cancels previous tasks instead of queuing multiple parallel runs for outdated values.

options.text: It cancels the current task and restarts a new task with the updated value.
options.explanation: Whenever the id value changes, SwiftUI cancels any active task and starts a fresh task.

options.text: It crashes the application if the previous task is still running.
options.explanation: SwiftUI cancels tasks cooperatively without throwing runtime crash exceptions.

options.text: It ignores the id change until the original network request finishes.
options.explanation: The task restarts immediately upon identity value change to prevent stale results.

questions.prompt: Explain how the SwiftUI .task modifier manages lifecycle and cancellation when a view appears and disappears.

rubric.criterion: Explains that .task launches an asynchronous task when the view appears
Explains that SwiftUI automatically cancels the running task when the view disappears
Notes that automatic cancellation prevents wasted network bandwidth, CPU time, and battery

questions.modelAnswer: The SwiftUI .task modifier automatically launches an asynchronous task when its attached view appears on screen. When the view disappears or is dismissed from navigation, SwiftUI cancels the running task cooperatively. This automatic cancellation prevents wasted cellular data, CPU cycles, and battery drain from background requests the user no longer needs.

questions.prompt: Describe how the .task(id:) modifier works and why it is useful for search or filter interfaces.

rubric.criterion: Explains that .task(id:) monitors changes to the provided identity value
Explains that SwiftUI cancels any active task before restarting a fresh task for the new value
Explains that this prevents race conditions where an old query could overwrite newer search results

questions.modelAnswer: The .task(id:) modifier re-executes whenever its equatable identity parameter changes. When a user modifies a search query or filter tab, SwiftUI cancels the currently active in-flight task before launching a fresh one. This prevents race conditions where an earlier, slower network response could arrive late and overwrite the newest search results.

questions.prompt: What are the three cases of AsyncImagePhase and what should a view render for each case?

rubric.criterion: Identifies .empty and describes rendering a loading indicator such as ProgressView
Identifies .success(Image) and describes rendering the downloaded image with modifiers like resizable
Identifies .failure(Error) and describes rendering an error icon or fallback placeholder

questions.modelAnswer: AsyncImagePhase defines three distinct cases. The .empty case indicates that the download is currently in flight, where views typically render a ProgressView spinner. The .success case delivers the loaded Image, which can be styled with modifiers like resizable and scaledToFit. The .failure case provides the underlying error, allowing developers to show an error symbol or fallback placeholder.

questions.prompt: Why might a senior iOS engineer choose a custom image caching pipeline over AsyncImage in a high-volume feed?
questions.lessonSection: How to answer in the interview

rubric.criterion: Mentions that AsyncImage relies primarily on URLCache without custom memory bounds
Explains the need for image downsampling to match view dimensions and prevent memory spikes
Discusses prefetching or persistent disk cache policies for smooth high-volume scrolling feeds

questions.modelAnswer: AsyncImage relies on Foundation URLCache, which lacks granular memory limits and downsampling capabilities. In a high-volume scrolling feed, decoding full-resolution photos into memory causes severe memory spikes and dropped frames. A senior engineer implements or integrates a pipeline with aggressive memory limits, background downsampling to view sizes, and prefetching.

questions.prompt: Why should you avoid creating unstructured Task blocks inside .onAppear to load view data?

rubric.criterion: Explains that unstructured tasks inside onAppear are not tied to view dismissal
Points out that the task continues downloading after the user navigates away
Notes that .task provides automatic cooperative cancellation upon view disappearance

questions.modelAnswer: Creating an unstructured Task inside .onAppear disconnects the asynchronous operation from the view presentation lifecycle. If a user quickly navigates away or closes the screen, the task continues running in the background, consuming cellular data and battery. In contrast, the .task modifier automatically binds execution to the view and cancels work cleanly when the view disappears.
